# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for AWS CPU instances
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoid interactive prompts from apt
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers, version control, and Open MPI
# This layer includes ca-certificates for secure network operations
# gfortran is removed as it is not a dependency
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# These settings improve compatibility and performance in environments like Kubernetes
# Allow running as root, which is common in containers
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Disable shared memory mechanisms that can cause issues in some container runtimes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
# Exclude InfiniBand and problematic network interfaces
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl="^openib"
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude="lo,docker0"
# Allow oversubscription of CPU cores, a common practice in HPC/cloud environments
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# Set a temporary directory for building dependencies
WORKDIR /tmp

# Download, build, and install all third-party libraries (TPLs) in a single layer
# This reduces image size and improves build efficiency
RUN \
    # --- METIS 4.0.3 ---
    # Download and extract
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Build with specified flags to avoid compiler errors
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install METIS as its Makefile lacks an 'install' target
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    # --- HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    # Download and extract
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI support and required flags
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx && \
    # Build in parallel
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install to a standard system location
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    # --- MFEM 4.7 ---
    # Clone the repository
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    # Check out the specified version
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, linking against the TPLs we just installed
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # FIX: Explicitly pass MPI flag to install command to ensure parallel version is installed
    make install MFEM_USE_MPI=YES PREFIX=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove all source code and archives to keep the final image lean
    rm -rf metis-4.0.3 metis-4.0.3.tar.gz hypre-2.28.0 v2.28.0.tar.gz mfem && \
    # Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed libraries
    ldconfig

# Set the final application working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone, build, and install the Laghos application
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, linking against MFEM
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Copy the final executable to a directory on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Copy the required application data files into the WORKDIR
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    cd .. && \
    # Clean up the Laghos source code
    rm -rf Laghos

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  annotations:
    optimization-strategy: The last run with increased problem size (-rs 3) yielded
      a ~2.8x performance jump, reaching a FoM of 352.95. This indicates the application
      scales well with workload per core on the hpc7g.16xlarge instance. This attempt
      pushes this strategy further by increasing the problem size again with four
      serial refinements (-rs 4) to test the limits of this scaling.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -rs 4
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
    launcher: false
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 64

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# MiniCluster manifest for running a Laghos experiment on an AWS CPU instance.
# This manifest configures a single-pod Flux cluster to run the HPC application.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. Flux will wrap the command with `flux run -n 4`.
  # This will run 4 parallel processes within the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Do not automatically delete the MiniCluster pods upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs and output files.
  cleanup: false

  # Configure logging modes for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Strict mode ensures the job fails if there are any issues with log streaming.
    strict: true

  # Define the container specification for the MiniCluster pods.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      
      # The application command to be executed by Flux.
      # This runs the Laghos proxy application with problem type 1 (-p 1)
      # using the specified mesh file, which is expected to be in the working directory.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh

      # This flag MUST be false. The broker pod (rank 0) will submit the job,
      # and this spec will be used for all pods in the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

# MiniCluster manifest for running a Laghos experiment on an AWS CPU instance.
# This manifest corrects a command-line argument from a previous failed run.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
  # Optimization: Corrected the command-line argument for setting the kinematic order from '-o' to '-ok'.
  annotations:
    optimization-strategy: 'The previous run failed because the laghos application received an unrecognized option "-o 3". The application log shows the correct flag for setting the kinematic order is "-ok". This attempt corrects the command to use "-ok 3" to properly increase the polynomial order, which should increase computational intensity as intended.'
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. Kept at 64 to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Do not automatically delete the MiniCluster pods upon completion.
  cleanup: false
  # Configure logging modes for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Strict mode ensures the job fails if there are any issues with log streaming.
    strict: true
  # Flux-specific configurations for the framework itself.
  flux:
    container:
      # Specify an ARM-compatible image for the Flux view, as the hpc7g instance is ARM-based.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  # Pod-specific configurations.
  pod:
    # Schedule the MiniCluster pod on a specific AWS instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
  # Define the container specification for the MiniCluster pods.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # The application command to be executed by Flux.
      # Corrected '-o 3' to '-ok 3' to set the kinematic finite element order, fixing the previous error.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -rs 2 -ok 3
      # This flag MUST be false. The broker pod (rank 0) will submit the job,
      # and this spec will be used for all pods in the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false

# MiniCluster manifest for running a Laghos experiment on an AWS CPU instance.
# This manifest resolves an "Exec format error" by switching to an ARM64-compatible application container image.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
  # Optimization: The previous run failed with an 'Exec format error' due to an architecture mismatch. This attempt resolves the issue by using a presumed ARM64-compatible image tag (:laghos-arm64) to match the hpc7g.16xlarge node.
  annotations:
    optimization-strategy: "The previous run failed with an 'Exec format error' due to an architecture mismatch between the x86_64 application container and the ARM64 node. This attempt resolves the issue by using a presumed ARM64-compatible image tag (:laghos-arm64), allowing the test with increased computational intensity (-ok 3) to run on the selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance."
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. Kept at 64 to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Do not automatically delete the MiniCluster pods upon completion.
  cleanup: false
  # Configure logging modes for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Strict mode ensures the job fails if there are any issues with log streaming.
    strict: true
  # Flux-specific configurations for the framework itself.
  flux:
    container:
      # Specify an ARM-compatible image for the Flux view, as the hpc7g instance is ARM-based.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  # Pod-specific configurations.
  pod:

context.details:
Build laghos, building hyre, metis, and mfem from source first. 
You MUST install hypre 2.28.0 and disable fortran and add the --enable-bigint flag.
You MUST install metis 4.0.3 from https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz and add OPTFLAGS=-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration.
You MUST install mfem 4.7 and make parallel.
You MUST ensure all globbed files from ./data from the root of the laghos codebase are in the WORKDIR.

context.optimize: Run cube_311_hex.mesh with laghos in the pwd. You MUST maximize the Major kernels total rate (megadofs x time steps / second). You can add additional parameters to achieve that goal.
